defects: Conclusion is strengthened beyond gold: produced requires `M ⊗[R] Localization.away s ≃ₗ[Localization.away s] Localization.away s` (an explicit isomorphism to the ring itself, i.e. free of rank exactly one), whereas gold only requires `Free (Localization.Away r) (LocalizedModule.Away r M)` (mere freeness, with no rank fixed to one). These are not the same proposition; showing they coincide under the invertibility hypothesis would require an additional non-trivial rank-rigidity argument, not just unfolding definitions.

Uses the base-change tensor product `M ⊗[R] Localization.away s` as the localized module, instead of gold's `LocalizedModule.Away r M`. These are only canonically isomorphic (via a localization/tensor comparison lemma), not definitionally identical, so the conclusion is phrased over a different (though related) construction than gold's.

Replaces gold's abstract `Module.Invertible R M` typeclass hypothesis with an explicit second module `M'` and hypothesis `hinv : M ⊗[R] M' ≃ₗ[R] R`. This may be a legitimate unbundled form of the same invertibility notion, but there is no guarantee the actual (unseen) definition of `Module.Invertible` is exactly this existential statement (e.g. it could instead be defined canonically via the dual module `M →ₗ[R] R`), so equivalence of hypotheses cannot be confirmed.
